key_insight: A combined 3D CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict friction stir welding behavior in HDPE and identify process windows that avoid defects.
engineering_relevance: The study gives practical guidance for setting rotation speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating to improve weld quality, reduce plunge-force spikes, and stabilize thermal gradients in thermoplastic FSW.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model for temperature, force, flow, and void prediction
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series data
Process-map generation across rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched experiments well for void formation and thermo-mechanical response.
watch_item: The process map and model accuracy are based on a specific HDPE material system and tested parameter range, so transfer to other polymers or tool geometries may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
